summary: An Indologist, Minkowski studied at Harvard, University of Delhi, and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, the University of Iowa, Cornell University (1989–2006), and Oxford as Boden Professor of Sanskrit (2005–2023).

Morris worked in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He taught at Keio University as Professor of English Literature (1938), was a lecturer at the University of Tokyo and Tokyo University of Literature and Science, and served as a BBC controller (1943–1958).

Pinney is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He has held posts at University College London as professor of anthropology and visual culture (~2000), Northwestern University, Australian National University, University of Chicago, University of Cape Town, and Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, George studied at Columbia University under Royal W. Weiler (1965), as well as under Pema Gyaltsen and Geshe Wangyal. He later served as professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982).

Queen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Between approximately 1989 and 2018, he served at Harvard University as Dean of Students for Continuing Education and as a lecturer on the Study of Religion, Buddhism, and World Religions.

Jones works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held positions at the University of Oxford, served as Lecturer and Research Associate at the University of Cambridge (2019–2023), and became Assistant Professor at the University of Vienna in 2023.

Wallis, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied at the University of Rochester, University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and UC Berkeley under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt. He was a guest lecturer at Naropa University (attested 2020).

Becker worked in Indology and religious studies. He taught at the Missionsärztliches Institut Würzburg (~1922–1937), which he founded in 1923, and was Privatdozent für Missionswissenschaft at the University of Würzburg in 1925.

Li was an art historian and sinologist who studied at the University of Nanking and the University of Iowa. He taught English at Nanking (1943–1947), was an art history professor at Iowa (~1956–1966), and joined the University of Kansas faculty in 1966.
Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Minobusan University, attested as associate professor in 2015 and as former professor in 2026.

Gurung works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of British Columbia and McGill University, Gurung held teaching and assistant roles at both institutions, served at the Karmapa International Buddhist Institute (2004–2010), and was General Secretary of KIBS (2012–2015).

Tang was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University and National Central University under Jian Ouyang, Shuming Liang, and Thomé H. Fang. He taught at National Central University and was founding chairman and Chair Professor at CUHK (1963–1974).
Yen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. Yen earned a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello (attested 2004) and studied with Todd Brown, Chanyun, and Sheng Yen.
Tai specializes in linguistics, sinology, and Tibetology. Tai studied at the Graduate School of Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~2004–2008) and held a post at the University of Hong Kong.

Trungpa was active in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Khenpo Gangshar, Shechen Kongtrul, and at Oxford (1963). He served as spiritual advisor at the Young Lamas Home School (1959–1963) and founded Naropa University in 1973.

Chökyi Gyatso studied under Khakyab Dorje, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, while also teaching Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Chökyi Nyima studied under Dudjom Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Active in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, he studied at Rumtek Monastery and with teachers including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He became abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling in 1976 and founded the Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 1981.
Chökyi Nyinche studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Shechen Gyaltsab, and taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Chönyi Drolma is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo (all attested 2011).
